Why Do So Many Linux Users Prefer the Command Line to a GUI?

Lazy users learn the GUI so they don't have to learn the CLI.

REALLY lazy users learn the CLI so they don't have to reach for a mouse.

If you're good at using a CLI, you won't have issues with clicking through a GUI. But someone who only uses GUIs will be totally lost with CLI.

Sometimes you can save a lot of time on a task, if you know the right commands for writing a shell script. Nobody can write good shell scripts without being an experienced CLI user. If you only use GUIs, you will have no clue what is possible with shell scripts.

The main issue is that most GUI tools are pretty slow, non modular and just not very good. Take Nautilus, it's search function is extremely limited compared to find, it takes forever to display larger directories and in terms of general functionality it's completely bare bones. That doesn't mean that a GUI file-manager can't be useful, just the existing ones are rarely worth the effort. The Windows95 file manager for example was quite good until they ruined search functionality in later versions.
